report.summary: Chunk 3 of harness.py: arms aggregate, run_arms, detect_provider, _ask, run_tier2, load_baseline, snapshot_baseline, write_baseline (partial).
risks: run_tier2 | medium | _ask catches all Exception and returns empty string; silent failures may be indistinguishable from a model that truly cannot answer. | Add logging or distinguish between 'no answer' and 'error' in the return.

run_tier2 | low | detect_provider silently swallows all exceptions (bare except) and returns None; a transient network error is indistinguishable from no provider. | Log the exception or differentiate error types.

run_tier2 | low | _whole_repo_text is called twice per repo (once with cap_chars, once with cap_chars=None) which may be inefficient but is not a correctness bug. | Cache the full text alongside the truncated version.

handoff.purpose: Implements arms aggregation, run_arms, detect_provider, _ask, run_tier2, baseline I/O and snapshot_baseline.

claims.text: Tie-inclusive on purpose: a strict '>' here silently counted a BM25 tie as an A win, contradicting the 'C>=A' column header (report.py) and this function's own docstring ('if C ties or beats A ... that is reported loudly, not smoothed over'). recall_A==1.0 on every current hand_reachable task makes a strict C win impossible, so with '>' the tie case -- dumb retrieval matching the product at equal cost, the commercially damning one -- was the ONLY case that could ever fire and it was being absorbed into 'no'.
claims.why: The code uses 'recall_c >= recall_a' (line 574), which is tie-inclusive. The comment accurately describes the previous behavior with '>' and justifies the change to '>='.

claims.text: Model-free (recall via ``_recall``), offline, no LLM -- safe to run alongside Tier 1.
claims.why: run_arms calls eval_task_arms and _recall (not shown but referenced); no LLM calls are present in this function.

claims.text: See ``eval_task_arms`` for what each arm measures and ``by_provenance`` for the (never-blended) per-provenance-tier breakdown.
claims.why: eval_task_arms and by_provenance are not defined in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: Success = every expected substring appears (case-insensitive). Also return the fraction present for a softer signal.
claims.why: Code checks all substrings (case-insensitive) and returns fraction.

claims.text: Only a local Ollama HTTP endpoint is probed (free, no key, no egress). The probe is a 2s GET to /api/tags -- it does nothing unless Tier 2 is requested.
claims.why: Code uses urllib.request.urlopen with timeout=2 to GET /api/tags on localhost.

claims.text: Single text-only turn against the provider. Never raises to the caller.
claims.why: Function catches all exceptions (bare except) and returns empty string; never raises.

claims.text: B's tokens were ALREADY measured with the real tokenizer before this change (``count_tokens`` is exact whenever tiktoken is installed) -- that part was honest.
claims.why: No evidence of previous behavior in this chunk; claim refers to state before this change.

claims.text: B is capped at ``cap_tokens * 4`` chars before being measured, so ``tokens_B`` silently reflected a TRUNCATED text, not the real whole-repo size.
claims.why: Code uses _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars) where cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4.

claims.text: ``tokens_B_true`` (added here) is the untruncated whole-repo token count, so a truncated B can never be mistaken for the real baseline.
claims.why: Code computes whole_true_tokens_cache[repo] = count_tokens(full_text) and includes tokens_B_true in per-task dict.

claims.text: Cleanly skipped (never crashes) when no provider is up.
claims.why: If detect_provider returns None, function returns a skipped dict immediately.

claims.text: Read baseline.json, or an empty baseline if it does not exist yet (a fresh repo checkout before the first ``--update-baseline`` run).
claims.why: Code checks os.path.exists(p); if not, returns {'schema': 1, 'tasks': {}}.

claims.text: Pure: build the baseline structure for the CURRENT recall of ``tasks`` (default TASKS). Does not touch disk -- see ``write_baseline``.
claims.why: Function calls run_tier1, builds dict, returns; no file I/O.

claims.text: Every task is snapshotted (including quarantine ones) so quarantine promotion is still comparable later; only PRIMARY tasks are ever gated (see ``run_gate``).
claims.why: run_gate is not in this chunk; cannot verify gating logic.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (``run_tier1``) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a 'new task' (not silently a pass) the next time ``run_gate`` sees them resolve successfully. FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no ``recall`` key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder 'never measured' into 'passing'.
claims.why: Code filters per_task: only includes tasks without 'error' and not focus_withheld.

claims.text: EXPLICIT-ONLY baseline write. Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op. Only the '--update-baseline' CLI flag (a human decision) should reach this. Returns the path written. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys) so the diff is meaningful in review.
claims.why: Function body is truncated; cannot verify formatting or return statement.

observations.what: run_tier2 calls _whole_repo_text twice per repo (once with cap_chars, once with None). This is inefficient but not incorrect.
detect_provider catches all exceptions with bare except, which may hide network errors.
_ask catches all exceptions and returns empty string; no distinction between 'no answer' and 'error'.
